The **Orlando Magic** are an American professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") team based in [Orlando, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida"). The Magic compete in the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA) as a member of the [Southeast Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Division_(NBA) "Southeast Division (NBA)") of the [Eastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Conference_(NBA) "Eastern Conference (NBA)"). The franchise was established in 1989 as an [expansion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expansion_team "Expansion team") franchise. Notable NBA stars as [Shaquille O'Neal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaquille_O'Neal "Shaquille O'Neal"), [Penny Hardaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penny_Hardaway "Penny Hardaway"), [Grant Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Hill "Grant Hill"), [Tracy McGrady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_McGrady "Tracy McGrady"), and [Dwight Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Howard "Dwight Howard"), have played for the club throughout its history. As of today, the franchise has played in the [NBA playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_playoffs "NBA playoffs") 19 times in 37 seasons, and twice went to the [NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals"), in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_NBA_Finals "1995 NBA Finals") and [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NBA_Finals "2009 NBA Finals"), losing to the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets") and the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers"), respectively.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Orlando_Magic&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### 1985–1986: Team creation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Orlando_Magic&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 1985–1986: Team creation")]

In September 1985, [Orlando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida") businessman Jim L. Hewitt approached [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") general manager [Pat Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Williams_(basketball) "Pat Williams (basketball)") as they met in [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas") on his idea of bringing an NBA team to Orlando.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-9) Intrigued by the potential of an [Orlando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida")-based NBA team, Williams became the front man of the investment group one year later, after he left the 76ers.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-10) On June 19, 1986, the two held a news conference to announce their intention of seeking an NBA franchise.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-biz-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-champ-12)

At the same time, Hewitt and Williams decided to hold a contest in the _[Orlando Sentinel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando\_Sentinel "Orlando Sentinel")_ newspaper to get names for their new franchise. Out of a total of 4,296 submitted entries, the names were subsequently narrowed to four, "Heat", "Tropics", "Juice", and "Magic". The last one, which had been submitted by 11 people, was picked after Williams brought his seven-year-old daughter [Karyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karyn_Williams "Karyn Williams") to visit in Orlando.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-MAGIC:_Behind_the_Name:_the_Orlando_Magic-13) On July 27, 1986, it was announced that the committee chose the Magic to be the new name of the Orlando franchise in the NBA.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-MAGIC:_20_Years_Ago_Today_%E2%80%93_The_Magic_Begins-14) The name "Magic" alludes to the area's biggest tourist attraction and economic engine [Walt Disney World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_World "Walt Disney World"), along with its [Magic Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_Kingdom "Magic Kingdom"), highlighting its [corporate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company") theme of [magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_(supernatural) "Magic (supernatural)"). Hewitt added that "You look at all the aspects of [Central Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Florida "Central Florida"), and you find it really is an exciting place, a magical place."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-17)

Many, including Williams [himself](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himself "Himself") at first, thought that [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami") or [Tampa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa "Tampa") were better locations in Florida for a franchise. At the time, Orlando was a small city without a major airport or a suitable arena.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-stern-18) Hewitt brought investors such as real estate developer William duPont, [Orlando Renegades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Renegades "Orlando Renegades") owner Don Dizney, and Southern Fruit Citrus owners Jim and Steve Caruso,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-biz-11) and talked the Orlando city officials into approving an arena project.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-19) Meanwhile, Williams gave presentations to [NBA commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commissioner_of_the_NBA "Commissioner of the NBA")[David Stern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Stern "David Stern") and the owners of the other teams of the league that the town was viable.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-stern-18)

In April, the franchise committee recommended expanding by three teams, with two of the slots going to [Charlotte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte,_North_Carolina "Charlotte, North Carolina") and [Minneapolis-St. Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minneapolis-St._Paul "Minneapolis-St. Paul"). The recommendation put the Orlando bid in doubt, since it advised that the state of [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida") should only be allocated one team as part of the three-team expansion. This feedback put the planned Orlando franchise up against the Miami-based team, originally known as the _Florida Heat_ and eventually named the [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-sunsentinel-20) When both Miami and Orlando ownership groups made successful pitches, the expansion committee decided to expand by four teams, allowing both to have a franchise.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-NYTexp-21)

The Magic became the first-ever major-league professional sports franchise in the Orlando area, following an expansion fee of reportedly $32.5 million.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-biz-11)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-NYTexp-21) They were one of the four new expansion franchises awarded by the NBA in 1987 along with the [Charlotte Hornets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Hornets "Charlotte Hornets"), [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat") and [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-22) The Magic hired [Matt Guokas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Guokas "Matt Guokas") as the team's first coach, who helped the Magic select 12 players in the [NBA expansion draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_NBA_expansion_draft "1989 NBA expansion draft") on June 15, 1989.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-23)

### 1989–1992: Early years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Orlando_Magic&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1989–1992: Early years")]

The Magic, in their debut year, selected [Nick Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Anderson_(basketball) "Nick Anderson (basketball)") from Illinois in the first round of the [1989 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_NBA_draft "1989 NBA draft"). As the 11th pick, he was the team's first franchise player and leading scorer for a decade. The Magic's very first game played was an exhibition game on October 13, 1989, against the then-reigning champion Detroit Pistons, which the Magic won.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-24) Anderson was quoted as saying the atmosphere and the people watching the game was "like Game 7 of the NBA Finals".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-Magic_history-25)

On November 4, 1989, the Magic played their first season game at the [Orlando Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Arena "Orlando Arena") (O-Rena) against the visiting [New Jersey Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Nets "New Jersey Nets"), who won 111–106 in a hard-fought game.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-26) The Magic's first victory came two days later, as the Magic defeated the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks") 118–110.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-27) The inaugural team compiled a record of 18–64 with players including the franchise star player [Nick Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Anderson_(basketball) "Nick Anderson (basketball)"), [Reggie Theus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie_Theus "Reggie Theus"), [Scott Skiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Skiles "Scott Skiles"), [Terry Catledge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Catledge "Terry Catledge"), [Sam Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Vincent_(basketball) "Sam Vincent (basketball)"), [Otis Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otis_Smith_(basketball) "Otis Smith (basketball)"), and [Jerry Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Reynolds_(basketball_player) "Jerry Reynolds (basketball player)").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-1989%E2%80%9390_Standings-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-NBA_Expansion_Drafts:_Results-29)

In the [1990 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_NBA_draft "1990 NBA draft"), the Orlando Magic selected [Dennis Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Scott_(basketball) "Dennis Scott (basketball)") with the fourth overall pick.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-30) On December 30, 1990, Scott Skiles racked up 30 assists in the 155–116 victory over the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets"), breaking [Kevin Porter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Porter_(basketball,_born_1950) "Kevin Porter (basketball, born 1950)")'s NBA single-game assists record (29).[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-31) Skiles was named the NBA's [Most Improved Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Most_Improved_Player_Award "NBA Most Improved Player Award") at the end of the season, as the Magic heralded the NBA's most improved record that season. Forward Dennis Scott set a team mark with 125 three-point field goals for the season, the best long-distance production by a rookie in NBA history.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-Magic_history-25) He was named to the [NBA All-Rookie First Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_All-Rookie_Team "NBA All-Rookie Team").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-Magic_history-25)

On September 19, 1991, the DeVos family, founders of [Amway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amway "Amway"), purchased the franchise for $85 million. Family patriarch [Richard DeVos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_DeVos "Richard DeVos") became the owner of the franchise.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-N.B.A._Orlando_Team_Sold-32) The [1991–92 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991%E2%80%9392_NBA_season "1991–92 NBA season") was disappointing for the Magic as various players missed games with injuries. Dennis Scott played only 18 games, Nick Anderson missed 22 games, [Stanley Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Roberts "Stanley Roberts"), Jerry Reynolds, [Brian Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bison_Dele "Bison Dele"), Sam Vincent and Otis Smith all missed at least 27 games each. With a shortage of healthy players, the team struggled through a 17-game losing streak and finished with a 21–61 record. The Magic still managed to have all 41 home games sold out.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-Magic_history-25)

### 1992–1996: The Shaquille O'Neal and Penny Hardaway era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Orlando_Magic&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1992–1996: The Shaquille O'Neal and Penny Hardaway era")]

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Shaquille_O%27Neal_1998.jpg/250px-Shaquille_O%27Neal_1998.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shaquille_O'Neal_1998.jpg)

Shaquille O’ Neal in 1998

The Magic’s history was changed on May 17, 1992, when the franchise won the first pick in the [1992 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_NBA_draft "1992 NBA draft") Lottery.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-Magic_history-25) The Magic selected big-man [Shaquille O'Neal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaquille_O'Neal "Shaquille O'Neal") from [Louisiana State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_State_University "Louisiana State University"), the biggest prize in the draft since the Knicks won [Patrick Ewing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Ewing "Patrick Ewing").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-The_Top_Pick_Is_Going_to_Disney_World-33) O'Neal, a 7 ft 1 in (2.16 m)[center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_(basketball) "Center (basketball)"), made an immediate impact on the Magic, leading the team to a 41–41 record.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-1992%E2%80%9393_Standings-34) The Magic again became the NBA's most improved franchise, as they improved by 20 games. O'Neal was the first rookie to be voted an All-Star starter since [Michael Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jordan "Michael Jordan") in 1985.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-Magic_history-25) He also became the 1992–93 [NBA Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Rookie_of_the_Year_Award "NBA Rookie of the Year Award"). Despite O'Neal's presence, the Magic missed the [1993 NBA playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_NBA_playoffs "1993 NBA playoffs") because they were tied with the [Indiana Pacers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Pacers "Indiana Pacers") for the eighth and final playoff spot in the Eastern Conference with the Pacers holding the tiebreaker.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-grantland-35)

Despite barely missing the playoffs and receiving the least chance of gaining the top draft pick with only one ball in the lottery, the Magic again won the first pick in the [1993 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_NBA_draft "1993 NBA draft") Lottery.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-Magic_history-25) Prior to the draft, Guokas stepped down as head coach, and [Brian Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Hill_(basketball_coach) "Brian Hill (basketball coach)") was promoted to become the Magic's second head coach.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-Hill_Is_Named_Coach_of_Magic-36) In the draft, the Magic selected [Chris Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Webber "Chris Webber"), but traded him to the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors") for the number three pick, guard [Penny Hardaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penny_Hardaway "Penny Hardaway") and three future first-round draft picks.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-Warriors_in_talks_with_Webber-37) With the combination of O'Neal and Hardaway, the Magic became a dominant team in the NBA, compiling the first 50 win season in franchise history with a 50–32 record.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-1993%E2%80%9394_Standings-38) The Magic were in the playoffs for the first time, ranked the fourth seed in the Eastern Conference; however, the Pacers swept the Magic 3–0 in the first round, thus ending the Magic's season.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-1994_Playoff_Results-39)

In the [1994–95 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994%E2%80%9395_NBA_season "1994–95 NBA season"), the Magic's sixth season, [All-Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NBA_All-Stars "List of NBA All-Stars") forward [Horace Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace_Grant "Horace Grant") was acquired as a [free agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_agent "Free agent") from the [Chicago Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-Magic_history-25) The Orlando Magic compiled a 57–25 record, best in the East and winning the [Atlantic Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Division_(NBA) "Atlantic Division (NBA)") title,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-1994%E2%80%9395_Standings-40) becoming the second-fastest team (behind the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks") in [1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_NBA_Finals "1971 NBA Finals"), who were in their third season) to advance to the NBA Finals in league history.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-Orlando_Magic:_Did_You_Know?-41) In the playoffs, the Magic defeated the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics"), Bulls, and the Pacers, advancing to the NBA Finals where O'Neal, Hardaway and the young Magic bowed to a more playoff-experienced [Hakeem Olajuwon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hakeem_Olajuwon "Hakeem Olajuwon") and the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets"), winning their second consecutive championship in a 4–0 sweep of Orlando.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-1995_Playoff_Results-42)

In the [1995–96 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995%E2%80%9396_NBA_season "1995–96 NBA season"), the Magic again were near the top of the Eastern Conference and the Atlantic Division with a 60–22 record, led by O'Neal and Hardaway; however, the Magic were seeded number two, behind the NBA's second-best all-time 72–10 record of the Chicago Bulls.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-1995%E2%80%9396_Standings-43) In the meantime, general manager Pat Williams was promoted to senior executive vice president and replaced by the vice president of Basketball Operations [John Gabriel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Gabriel_(basketball) "John Gabriel (basketball)") on April 29, 1996.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-MAGIC:_All-Time_Transactions-44) In the playoffs, after the Magic defeated the [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons") and the [Atlanta Hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Hawks "Atlanta Hawks"), Orlando met the Bulls in the Eastern Conference Finals.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-1996_Playoff_Results-45) The combination of Jordan, [Scottie Pippen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Pippen "Scottie Pippen") and rebounder [Dennis Rodman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Rodman "Dennis Rodman") was too much for the Magic, and Orlando was swept 4–0.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-46)

### 1996–1999: The post-Shaq/Penny Hardaway era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Orlando_Magic&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1996–1999: The post-Shaq/Penny Hardaway era")]

In the off-season, O'Neal left as a [free agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_agent "Free agent") to the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers"), dealing a huge blow to the Magic franchise.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-47) In the middle of the season, urged by player discontent, management fired coach [Brian Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Hill_(basketball) "Brian Hill (basketball)") and named [Richie Adubato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richie_Adubato "Richie Adubato") as interim coach for the rest of the season.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-48) Under Adubato, the Magic went 21–12 to compile a 45–37 record, led by [Penny Hardaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penny_Hardaway "Penny Hardaway"). In the playoffs, the Magic quickly fell 0–2 to the heavily favored Miami Heat in the first round, but Hardaway battled back with consecutive 40-point games to assure a game five (the first player to do so), which the Magic ultimately lost.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-grantland-35)

The Magic then hired [Chuck Daly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Daly "Chuck Daly") to be head coach for the [1997–98 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997%E2%80%9398_NBA_season "1997–98 NBA season").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-49) In addition, Hall of Famer [Julius Erving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Erving "Julius Erving") joined the Magic's front office, giving Orlando hope for a successful season.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-50) The season was hampered by an injury to Hardaway who sat out the majority of the season. Anderson, combined with newly acquired free agent [Bo Outlaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Outlaw "Bo Outlaw"), led the team to a 41–41 record, just out of reach of the NBA playoffs. In addition, [Rony Seikaly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rony_Seikaly "Rony Seikaly") was traded during the season to the [New Jersey Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Nets "New Jersey Nets") for three role players and a future draft pick.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-51)

In [1998–99](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998%E2%80%9399_NBA_season "1998–99 NBA season"), with the drafting of [Michael Doleac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Doleac "Michael Doleac") and [Matt Harpring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Harpring "Matt Harpring") with the 12th and 15th picks in the [1998 draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_NBA_Draft "1998 NBA Draft"), and a healthy Penny Hardaway and Nick Anderson, the Magic tied for the Eastern Conference's best record with the [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat") in the lockout-shortened season, 33–17. At the heart of the team was veteran and future Orlando Magic Hall of Famer [Darrell Armstrong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darrell_Armstrong "Darrell Armstrong"), leading from the vanguard (a constant that Orlando fans would enjoy for a decade) and picking up the NBA's [Sixth-Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixth-Man "Sixth-Man") and [Most Improved Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Most_Improved_Player_Award "NBA Most Improved Player Award") awards along the way.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-53) Orlando also acquired NBA great [Dominique Wilkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominique_Wilkins "Dominique Wilkins"), along with brother Gerald, who were past their primes but were both still serviceable NBA players.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-54) In the playoffs the Penny Hardaway-led Magic were seeded number 3 because of tiebreakers and faced the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers"). The 76ers, led by [Allen Iverson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Iverson "Allen Iverson"), upset the Magic 3–1 in the first round.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-55) The team also changed their uniforms for the first time ever, changing from pinstripes to stars.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-56)

### 1999–2000: "Heart and Hustle" season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Orlando_Magic&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1999–2000: \"Heart and Hustle\" season")]

In 1999, the Magic, under general manager [John Gabriel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Gabriel_(basketball) "John Gabriel (basketball)"), who was later named Executive of the Year, hired rookie-coach [Doc Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_Rivers "Doc Rivers").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-57) Gabriel dismantled the previous team trading their only remaining superstar Penny Hardaway to the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") for [Danny Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Manning "Danny Manning") (who never donned a Magic uniform), [Pat Garrity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Garrity "Pat Garrity"), and two future draft picks.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-58) The Magic were then a team composed of virtually all no name players and little experience, which included team captain Armstrong, Bo Outlaw and a young [Ben Wallace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Wallace_(basketball) "Ben Wallace (basketball)"), along with Coach Rivers, who led the Magic to a 41–41 record, barely missing out on the playoffs. At the end of the season Rivers was named [Coach of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Coach_of_the_Year "NBA Coach of the Year"). That year was characterized by the slogan "Heart and Hustle", as the team was known for its hard-working style.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-59)

### 2000–2004: The Tracy McGrady era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Orlando_Magic&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2000–2004: The Tracy McGrady era")]

The following off-season, Gabriel, with millions of cleared salary cap space, attempted to lure three of the NBA's most prized free agents: [Tim Duncan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Duncan "Tim Duncan"), [Grant Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Hill_(basketball) "Grant Hill (basketball)"), and [Tracy McGrady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_McGrady "Tracy McGrady"). While Duncan opted to remain with the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs"), the Magic acquired Hill,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-60) a perennial All-Star, and McGrady.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-61) With McGrady and Hill together, the Magic were expected to be a force in the East. However, Hill was limited to 4 games because of an ankle injury. McGrady blossomed into a star during the season, becoming one of the NBA's top scorers. With the addition of [Mike Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Miller_(basketball,_born_1980) "Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)") from the draft, the Magic compiled a 43–39 record, which included a nine-game winning streak, and once again made the playoffs. McGrady made the All-Star Team and All-NBA Second Team. Miller won the [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Rookie_of_the_Year_Award "NBA Rookie of the Year Award").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-62) In the playoffs, they faced the Milwaukee Bucks in the first round. The Bucks won the series 3–1.

In [2001–02](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001%E2%80%9302_NBA_season "2001–02 NBA season"), McGrady led the Magic to a winning record of 44–38. Hill was still severely limited by his ankle injury, and did not play for the vast majority of the season. McGrady, combined with Armstrong, Miller, and 3-point sharpshooter [Pat Garrity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Garrity "Pat Garrity"), formed the core of the team. McGrady made the All-NBA for the first time and made his second consecutive All-Star Team. However, the Magic were defeated 3–1 in the first round of the playoffs by the [Charlotte Hornets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Hornets "Charlotte Hornets") led by [Baron Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baron_Davis "Baron Davis").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-63)

In [2002–03](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_NBA_season "2002–03 NBA season"), with the acquisitions of [Gordan Giricek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordan_Giricek "Gordan Giricek") and [Drew Gooden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drew_Gooden_(basketball) "Drew Gooden (basketball)") from the [Memphis Grizzlies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Grizzlies "Memphis Grizzlies") in exchange for [Mike Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Miller_(basketball,_born_1980) "Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)"), McGrady once again led the Magic to a 42–40 record. McGrady led the league in scoring with 32.1 points per game, made his second All-NBA First Team, and Third All-Star Team. Despite still not having Hill due to injury, the Magic entered the playoffs for the third straight year. However, after taking a 3–1 lead in the best-of-seven first-round series, the Magic fell to the [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons") 4–3. McGrady was quoted as saying, "It feels good to get in the second round" after still needing one more win to advance.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-64)

The Magic's 15th season in [2003–04](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_NBA_season "2003–04 NBA season") proved to be one of its toughest ever. Even with the acquisition of veteran free agents [Tyronn Lue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyronn_Lue "Tyronn Lue") and [Juwan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juwan_Howard "Juwan Howard"), the Magic struggled early. After winning its first game, the Magic lost 19 consecutive games, setting a franchise record. They never recovered, and finished an NBA worst 21–61. Despite this, McGrady led the league in scoring with 28.0 points per game, made the All-NBA Second Team and his fourth consecutive All-Star Team. In the middle of the 19-game losing streak, coach Doc Rivers was fired, and assistant [Johnny Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Davis_(basketball,_born_1955) "Johnny Davis (basketball, born 1955)") was promoted to head coach.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-65) General manager Gabriel was replaced by [John Weisbrod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Weisbrod "John Weisbrod").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-66)

### 2004–2012: The Dwight Howard era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Orlando_Magic&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2004–2012: The Dwight Howard era")]

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/Dwight_Howard.jpg/250px-Dwight_Howard.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dwight_Howard.jpg)

[Dwight Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Howard "Dwight Howard") was drafted No. 1 overall in the [2004 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NBA_draft "2004 NBA draft").

In the off-season, Weisbrod completely dismantled the team. Though he kept Davis as coach, he shook up the player roster, only keeping a few players from last season. The most significant trade was [Tracy McGrady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_McGrady "Tracy McGrady"). McGrady, discontent with the Magic, wished to move on; Weisbrod accused McGrady of "slacking off" and not attending practices (McGrady later admitted that he did not give 100 percent during the 2003–04 season and wanted the team to bring him some help, but never wanted to leave Orlando). The Magic traded McGrady along with [Reece Gaines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reece_Gaines "Reece Gaines"), [Tyronn Lue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyronn_Lue "Tyronn Lue"), and [Juwan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juwan_Howard "Juwan Howard") to the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets") for [Steve Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Francis "Steve Francis"), [Kelvin Cato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvin_Cato "Kelvin Cato"), and [Cuttino Mobley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuttino_Mobley "Cuttino Mobley").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-67) In addition, the Magic acquired center [Tony Battie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Battie "Tony Battie") and two second-round draft picks from the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers") in exchange for Drew Gooden, [Steven Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Hunter "Steven Hunter"), and the draft rights to [Anderson Varejão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderson_Varej%C3%A3o "Anderson Varejão").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-68) The Magic then signed free agent [Hedo Türkoğlu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedo_T%C3%BCrko%C4%9Flu "Hedo Türkoğlu"). With the number one draft pick, the Magic selected high-school phenomenon and future All-Star and franchise cornerstone [Dwight Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Howard "Dwight Howard"), and a draft-day trade with the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets") got them point guard [Jameer Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jameer_Nelson "Jameer Nelson").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-0405s-69)

After a promising 13–6 start, the Magic began to fall apart. First, Weisbrod traded Mobley for [Doug Christie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doug_Christie "Doug Christie") from the [Sacramento Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings"). Christie, because of his emotional ties to the Kings, at first refused to play for the Magic. Later on, Christie claimed he had [bone spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_spur "Bone spur") and was placed on the injured list after playing only a few games for the Magic.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-70) Near the end of the season, with a playoff-push faltering, Weisbrod fired Davis after leading Davis to believe he was going to be the team's head coach for the entire [2004–05 NBA season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_NBA_season "2004–05 NBA season"). He then promoted [Chris Jent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Jent "Chris Jent") to interim head coach.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-71) Throughout the season, bolstered by Hill's return, the Magic played spectacularly, defeating top NBA teams. However, led by the erratic play of Francis, the Magic also lost to league teams with losing records. Howard showed great promise, becoming one of the few players to average a double-double. Howard was a consistent rebounder and scorer, becoming the first rookie to start and play all 82 games in a season. In addition, Nelson, after a slow start, developed into a talented player, taking over the starting point guard position. Hill also returned and averaged 19.7 points a game. Hill was chosen an All-Star starter by NBA fans for the 2005 All-Star Game, and Dwight Howard and Jameer Nelson were named to the All-Rookie first and second teams, respectively. Howard was a unanimous selection.

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/J.J._RedickJameer_Nelson.jpg/250px-J.J._RedickJameer_Nelson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:J.J._RedickJameer_Nelson.jpg)

[Jameer Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jameer_Nelson "Jameer Nelson") spent 10 seasons with Orlando from 2004 to 2014.

The Magic finished the season 36–46.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-0405s-69) Their playoff push was hampered by injuries in the last quarter of the season: a season-ending broken wrist for sixth man [Hedo Türkoğlu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedo_T%C3%BCrko%C4%9Flu "Hedo Türkoğlu"), a shin injury to [Grant Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Hill_(basketball) "Grant Hill (basketball)"), a rib cage injury to Nelson, and a three-game suspension to Francis for kicking a photographer. The Magic ended a few games out of the playoffs. On May 23, 2005, the Magic's plans were disrupted by the abrupt resignation of general manager and Chief Operating Officer [John Weisbrod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Weisbrod "John Weisbrod").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-72) In addition, the Magic announced the following day that [Brian Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Hill_(basketball_coach) "Brian Hill (basketball coach)"), the coach who led the Magic to the [NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals") under O'Neal and Hardaway, would return as head coach.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-73)

The Magic drafted [Fran Vázquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran_V%C3%A1zquez "Fran Vázquez") with the 11th pick in the [2005 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_NBA_draft "2005 NBA draft"). On July 28, 2005, Vazquez stunned the team after announcing that he would remain in Spain to play for [Akasvayu Girona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akasvayu_Girona "Akasvayu Girona"), getting ridiculed by media after he was quoted that the decision to stay was made by his girlfriend.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-74) Owner [Rich DeVos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rich_DeVos "Rich DeVos") announced on October 21 that he was transferring ownership to his children, with the official owner role moving to son-in-law and team president Bob Vander Weide. The transfer was supposed to be complete by the end of the year.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-75)

The [2005–06 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_NBA_season "2005–06 NBA season") opened with high hopes for the Magic despite not being able to add first-round draft pick Vasquez. Grant Hill was supposedly finally healed from his multiple ankle surgeries. [Dwight Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Howard "Dwight Howard") and [Jameer Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jameer_Nelson "Jameer Nelson") showed excellent progress during summer-league play. Second-round draft pick [Travis Diener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travis_Diener "Travis Diener") showed excellent shooting and decision-making during the summer. And the free-agent signing of [Keyon Dooling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keyon_Dooling "Keyon Dooling") showed that the club was going to continue making progress. Then trouble began. Hill, despite his ankle apparently being healed, suffered a painful sports hernia injury that would hamper his play throughout the entire season. After playing in three preseason games, he underwent surgery to correct the hernia and would not appear during the regular season until mid-December, to which he lasted a month before attempting to make another comeback in February and early March, however, he only played sporadically. Then a foot injury to Nelson forced him to sit out for over a month.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-76)

On February 15, 2006, the Magic announced that they had acquired [Darko Miličić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darko_Mili%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Darko Miličić") and [Carlos Arroyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Arroyo "Carlos Arroyo") from the [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons") in exchange for [Kelvin Cato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvin_Cato "Kelvin Cato") and a [2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_NBA_draft "2007 NBA draft") top-five protected first-round draft pick.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-77) One week later, on February 22, the Magic announced that they had traded [Steve Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Francis "Steve Francis") to the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks") in exchange for [Penny Hardaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penny_Hardaway "Penny Hardaway") (whom they waived two days later) and [Trevor Ariza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Ariza "Trevor Ariza").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-78) With a set starting rotation of Battie, Howard, Türkoğlu, [DeShawn Stevenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeShawn_Stevenson "DeShawn Stevenson"), and Nelson, the Magic mounted a surprising run at the eighth playoff spot in the Eastern Conference, including an 8-game winning streak and 12 consecutive home wins. The streak included wins against NBA powerhouses Detroit, San Antonio, Dallas and Miami, as well as a game against the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") in which Howard recorded 28 points and a career-high 26 rebounds. Despite their efforts they did not make the playoffs.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-79)

#### 2006–2010: Return to the NBA Finals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Orlando_Magic&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2006–2010: Return to the NBA Finals")]

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Stan_Van_Gundy_sideline_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Stan_Van_Gundy_sideline_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Stan_Van_Gundy_sideline_(cropped).jpg)

Head coach [Stan Van Gundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Van_Gundy "Stan Van Gundy")

With the 11th overall pick in the [2006 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_NBA_draft "2006 NBA draft"), the Magic took former Duke star [JJ Redick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JJ_Redick "JJ Redick"). Even with the fan support to get him playing time he averaged just over 11 minutes a game. After beginning the season strong with a 13–4 record, the Orlando Magic began to suffer in the standings as the result of multiple losses, due in large part to the injuries of Tony Battie, Keyon Dooling, and Grant Hill. The Magic were also hampered with the sporadic play of many of their young stars, who on multiple occasions showed their propensity for streaky shooting and the team's lack of a solid scoring two-guard. Despite the team's poor play, Dwight Howard continued to develop and blossom in his third year in the league, culminating in his first selection to the Eastern Conference All-Star team. The final few weeks of the season saw the Magic build momentum and confidence with an impressive late push towards the Playoffs. On April 15, 2007, with an 88–86 victory over the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics"), the Magic secured its first berth in the NBA playoffs since 2003 by locking up the eighth seed in the Eastern Conference. This marked the first time that the team had made the playoffs while posting a losing record. Nevertheless, their Playoff run ended on April 28, 2007, after they were swept in the first round by first seeded [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons") whose experience, veteran leadership and ability to consistently make the clutch basket proved far too much for the undermanned and overwhelmed Magic to overcome. It was announced on May 23, 2007, that [Brian Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Hill_(basketball_coach) "Brian Hill (basketball coach)") had been fired as head coach of the Magic.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-80)

On June 1, 2007, the Magic signed [Billy Donovan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Donovan "Billy Donovan") to be their head coach for five years. The next day, Donovan wished to be released from the contract and the Magic agreed several days later. On June 6, 2007, the Magic signed a 4-year contract with [Stan Van Gundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Van_Gundy "Stan Van Gundy"). In the [free agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_agent "Free agent") market, the Magic signed [Rashard Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashard_Lewis "Rashard Lewis") of the [Seattle SuperSonics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_SuperSonics "Seattle SuperSonics") to a six-year league-maximum contract believed to be worth over $110 million.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-81) At the NBA China Games, the Magic swept the three games in China, twice against the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers") and once against the Chinese national team in games held in Shanghai and in [Macau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macau "Macau").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-82)

On November 15, 2007, Bob Vander Weide, the son-in-law of Richard DeVos, officially took over as owner of the team, although ownership is still split evenly amongst Richard DeVos' other children as well.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-83)

The Magic started the [2007–08 NBA season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_NBA_season "2007–08 NBA season") with an impressive 16–4 record in their first 20 games, which included wins over the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") and [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers"). Through the next few months, the Magic were not so successful, splitting their next 36 games with 18 wins and 18 losses. At the start of March, the Magic seemed to pick up speed again, finishing the month with 10 wins, the first time since November that they won 10 or more in a month. The Magic clinched the [Southeast Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Division_(NBA) "Southeast Division (NBA)") title when the [Washington Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Wizards "Washington Wizards") were routed at [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Jazz "Utah Jazz") 129–87 on March 31, 2008. It was the Magic's third division title, but only their first since 1995–96 season, as well as their first since the Southeast Division was formed. They also earned their 50th win of the season against the [Chicago Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls") on April 13, which had not happened since the 1995–96 season. The Magic finished the regular season 52–30, their best season since 1995–96. With the third seed in the Eastern Conference, they were matched up in their first-round playoff series against the [Toronto Raptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Raptors "Toronto Raptors"). The Magic had home-court advantage for the first time since the 1998–99 season.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-84)

On April 28, 2008, at [Amway Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amway_Arena "Amway Arena"), the Magic eliminated the Raptors with a 4–1 series victory in the first round.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-85) It was the first playoff series victory for the Magic in 12 years after 6 straight first-round exits. The run of success did not last long as they fell 4–1 to the experienced [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons") in the second round.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-86) With the Magic already down in the series, controversy erupted after the Pistons' Game 2 victory. At the conclusion of the third quarter, [Chauncey Billups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chauncey_Billups "Chauncey Billups") of the Pistons made a three-point shot giving the Pistons a three-point lead. However, the clock had stopped just as the play began. NBA rules prohibit officials from using instant replay or any timing device to determine how much time has elapsed when a clock malfunctions, nor is a replay allowed to be viewed from the time of the malfunction to when the play ends, when the game clock has not expired. Because of the rule, the officials then estimated that the play took 4.6 seconds, and because there were 5.1 seconds remaining when play began, the field goal was allowed to be counted. The NBA later admitted that the play actually took 5.7 seconds and the basket in question should not have counted.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-87) The Pistons went on to win Game 2. The Magic were able to win Game 3, with the Pistons' Chauncey Billups out for most of the game with an injury but were unable to take advantage of his absence and defeat the Pistons in Games 4 and 5, which ended the Magic's playoff run in 2008. Another highlight of the season was [Hedo Turkoglu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedo_T%C3%BCrko%C4%9Flu "Hedo Türkoğlu") winning Most Improved Player.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-88)

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ab/J._J._Redick.jpg/250px-J._J._Redick.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:J._J._Redick.jpg)

[JJ Redick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JJ_Redick "JJ Redick") in 2008

The first half of the [2008–09 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_NBA_season "2008–09 NBA season") went very well for the Magic. After 41 games, the Magic were 33–8, leading the Southeast Division, as well as having one of the top four records in the league. At the start of February, [Jameer Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jameer_Nelson "Jameer Nelson"), their all-star starting point guard, went down with a shoulder injury. He was expected to miss the remainder of the season.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-89) After trading for [Rafer Alston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafer_Alston "Rafer Alston"), the Magic finished the regular season with a 59–23 record, it was the most games the team had won in a season since the 1995–96 season in which they had 60 wins. In the playoffs, the Magic beat the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") in the first round of the [playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NBA_playoffs "2009 NBA playoffs") and then the defending champions, the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics"), in the Eastern Conference semifinals, behind assistant coach [Patrick Ewing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Ewing "Patrick Ewing")'s guarantee that they would win Game 7 of that series.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-90) In their first conference finals since 1996, the Magic beat the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers"), which were led by the season's MVP, [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James"). After dropping the first two games in the [Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NBA_Finals "2009 NBA Finals") against the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers"), the Magic finally won their first-ever game in the Finals in Game 3. Despite Nelson's return to the team for the Finals, the Lakers won the series and the championship by beating the Magic in five games.

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Hedo_Turkoglu_point_guard_11-27-08.jpg/250px-Hedo_Turkoglu_point_guard_11-27-08.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hedo_Turkoglu_point_guard_11-27-08.jpg)

2007-08 Most Improved Player [Hedo Türkoğlu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedo_T%C3%BCrko%C4%9Flu "Hedo Türkoğlu") in 2008

In the 2009 off-season, Orlando traded [Rafer Alston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafer_Alston "Rafer Alston"), [Tony Battie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Battie "Tony Battie"), and [Courtney Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Courtney_Lee "Courtney Lee") to the [New Jersey Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Nets "New Jersey Nets") in exchange for eight-time [All-Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NBA_All-Stars "List of NBA All-Stars")[Vince Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Carter "Vince Carter") and [Ryan Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Anderson_(basketball,_born_1988) "Ryan Anderson (basketball, born 1988)").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-91)[Hedo Türkoğlu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedo_T%C3%BCrko%C4%9Flu "Hedo Türkoğlu"), as part of a [sign-and-trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sign-and-trade "Sign-and-trade"), was sent to the [Toronto Raptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Raptors "Toronto Raptors"). They then made several free agent signings. On July 10, former [Dallas Mavericks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Mavericks "Dallas Mavericks") power forward [Brandon Bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Bass "Brandon Bass") was given a 4-year deal.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-92) On July 21, the Magic signed former [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") forward [Matt Barnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Barnes "Matt Barnes").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-93) On August 19, they signed former [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat") point guard [Jason Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Williams_(basketball,_born_1975) "Jason Williams (basketball, born 1975)"), who decided to come back after a year in retirement.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-94)

On September 28, 2009, Orlando extended the contract of head coach [Stan Van Gundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Van_Gundy "Stan Van Gundy") by exercising his option for the 2010–11 season. They did the same for general manager [Otis Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otis_Smith_(basketball) "Otis Smith (basketball)"), which would keep him in that position through the 2011–12 season.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-95)

The Magic were without [Rashard Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashard_Lewis "Rashard Lewis") for the first 10 games of the [2009–10 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NBA_season "2009–10 NBA season"). Lewis tested positive for an elevated testosterone level that was caused by an over-the-counter supplement containing a substance banned by the league.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-Lewis_suspended_10_games_by_NBA-96) To make matters worse, Vince Carter suffered a left ankle injury in just the second game of the season. Carter's injury turned out to be not too serious, but caused him to miss the next five games. Another setback came in mid-November, when [Jameer Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jameer_Nelson "Jameer Nelson") injured his left knee, which required arthroscopic surgery to repair. Nelson would be out for five weeks. Despite all of this, the Magic had a 23–8 record at the end of December.

Orlando lost seven of their first ten games in January but recovered well enough to post a winning record for the month by winning six of their next seven. Following the All-Star break, the Magic went on a roll, winning 23 of their 28 remaining games, clinching their fourth consecutive playoff berth and winning their third consecutive division championship in the process. The Magic finished the regular season with a 59–23 record, matching their record from the 2008–09 season, and finishing with not only the second-best record in the Eastern Conference, but the second-best record in the entire league. The team became one of the only teams in NBA history to beat all of the other 29 teams at least once during the regular season. The Magic swept the [Charlotte Bobcats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Bobcats "Charlotte Bobcats") and the [Atlanta Hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Hawks "Atlanta Hawks") in the first two rounds of the [playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NBA_playoffs "2010 NBA playoffs"), respectively. They then faced the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") in the conference finals. After losing the first three games of the series, Orlando managed to win the next two games, but lost on the road in Game 6, ending their season.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-97)

#### 2010–2012: "Dwightmare" saga

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Orlando_Magic&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2010–2012: \"Dwightmare\" saga")]

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Scott_Skiles_bench_cropped.jpg/250px-Scott_Skiles_bench_cropped.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Scott_Skiles_bench_cropped.jpg)

[Scott Skiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Skiles "Scott Skiles") coached the Magic in the [2015–16 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_NBA_season "2015–16 NBA season").

In anticipation of the team's move to [Amway Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amway_Center "Amway Center"), the Magic updated its logo. They retained the streaking ball logo, but changed the wordmark taken from their current uniforms. The Magic hosted the NBA All-Star Game in 2012. The Magic also unveiled black alternate uniforms.

In the summer of 2010, the Orlando Magic signed [Chris Duhon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Duhon "Chris Duhon"), formerly of the New York Knicks,[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-98) and [Quentin Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quentin_Richardson "Quentin Richardson"), formerly of the Miami Heat.

On December 18, 2010, having lost five of their last six games, the Magic made a blockbuster trade deal with the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") and the [Washington Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Wizards "Washington Wizards"). They traded [Vince Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Carter "Vince Carter"), [Marcin Gortat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcin_Gortat "Marcin Gortat") and [Mickaël Piétrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micka%C3%ABl_Pi%C3%A9trus "Mickaël Piétrus") to Phoenix for [Hedo Türkoğlu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedo_T%C3%BCrko%C4%9Flu "Hedo Türkoğlu") (who led them into the 2009 NBA Finals when they lost 4–1 against the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers")), [Jason Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Richardson "Jason Richardson") and [Earl Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earl_Clark "Earl Clark"). [Rashard Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashard_Lewis "Rashard Lewis") was traded to Washington for 3-time All-Star [Gilbert Arenas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_Arenas "Gilbert Arenas").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-99)

The Magic finished the season with 52 victories, good for second in the Southeast Division. But they were ousted in six games by the [Atlanta Hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Hawks "Atlanta Hawks") in the first round of the [2011 NBA playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_playoffs "2011 NBA playoffs"), the first time head coach [Stan Van Gundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Van_Gundy "Stan Van Gundy") was eliminated early in the playoffs.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-100)

In a lockout-shortened [2011–12 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_NBA_season "2011–12 NBA season"), the Magic started the off-season on a rocky note, with their All-Star center, [Dwight Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Howard "Dwight Howard"), requesting a trade to either the [New Jersey Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Nets "New Jersey Nets"), [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers"), or [Dallas Mavericks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Mavericks "Dallas Mavericks"). Overlooking the trade request the Magic did a sign and trade with the Boston Celtics for [Glen Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glen_Davis_(basketball) "Glen Davis (basketball)") and [Von Wafer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Von_Wafer "Von Wafer") in exchange for [Brandon Bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Bass "Brandon Bass"). The Magic also amnestied [Gilbert Arenas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_Arenas "Gilbert Arenas") and signed [Larry Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Hughes "Larry Hughes"), [Justin Harper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Harper_(basketball) "Justin Harper (basketball)"), and [DeAndre Liggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeAndre_Liggins "DeAndre Liggins"). The Magic started the season on Christmas Day in [Oklahoma City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City "Oklahoma City") against the [Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City_Thunder "Oklahoma City Thunder"). They lost the season opener 97–89. During the month of February, the Magic waived Hughes and signed [Ish Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ish_Smith "Ish Smith"). On February 26, Orlando hosted the 2012 All-Star Game. The Magic struggled to win games consistently, with concerns about the uncertainty of Dwight Howard's future with the franchise. However, after Dwight rescinded his trade demand and signed a one-year deal in March, the Magic seemed to find their footing again. But then in early April, shortly after it became public that Howard requested coach Van Gundy to be replaced, the center was diagnosed with a herniated disk and forced to have back surgery, thus ending his season. The Magic clinched the sixth seed in the east with a 37–29 record. The Magic were faced with the third-seeded Pacers in the first round. Despite winning the first game of the series the Magic were defeated 4–1.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-101)

On May 21, 2012, it was reported that general manager [Otis Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otis_Smith_(basketball) "Otis Smith (basketball)") and head coach [Stan Van Gundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Van_Gundy "Stan Van Gundy") would part ways with the organization. Stan Van Gundy finished with a 259–135 regular season record with the team which included making the playoffs in those five years and a conference championship.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-102)

CEO [Alex Martins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Martins_(basketball) "Alex Martins (basketball)") announced former Oklahoma City assistant general manager [Rob Hennigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Hennigan "Rob Hennigan") as the new general manager for the Orlando Magic on June 20, 2012. Once hired, he became the youngest general manager in the league.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-103)

In the [2012 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_NBA_draft "2012 NBA draft"), the Magic selected [Andrew Nicholson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Nicholson_(basketball) "Andrew Nicholson (basketball)") and [Kyle O'Quinn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_O'Quinn "Kyle O'Quinn").[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-104)

On June 25, 2012, [Dwight Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Howard "Dwight Howard") had face-to-face meetings with general manager [Rob Hennigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Hennigan "Rob Hennigan") in Los Angeles and demanded a trade to the [Brooklyn Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Nets "Brooklyn Nets").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-105)

On July 9, 2012, the Magic completed a sign-and-trade deal with the [New Orleans Hornets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Hornets "New Orleans Hornets"), that sent forward Ryan Anderson to the Hornets. In return the Magic received center [Gustavo Ayon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustavo_Ayon "Gustavo Ayon").[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-106)

On July 28, 2012, [Jacque Vaughn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacque_Vaughn "Jacque Vaughn") was named the new head coach. He had been the assistant coach for the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs") for the last two seasons.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-107)

On August 9, 2012, [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN") reported that a four-team trade would send [Dwight Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Howard "Dwight Howard") to the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers"). Marc Stein of ESPN.com was told the Lakers were to acquire Howard, [Chris Duhon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Duhon "Chris Duhon") and [Earl Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earl_Clark "Earl Clark"), the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets") were to acquire [Andre Iguodala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Iguodala "Andre Iguodala"), the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") were to acquire [Andrew Bynum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Bynum "Andrew Bynum") and [Jason Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Richardson "Jason Richardson"), and the Magic were to acquire [Arron Afflalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arron_Afflalo "Arron Afflalo"), [Al Harrington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Harrington "Al Harrington"), [Nikola Vučević](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Vu%C4%8Devi%C4%87 "Nikola Vučević"), [Maurice Harkless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Harkless "Maurice Harkless"), [Josh McRoberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_McRoberts "Josh McRoberts"), [Christian Eyenga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Eyenga "Christian Eyenga"), and five total protected future (three first-round, two second-round) picks from each of the other three teams.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-108) The deal was officially confirmed and completed on August 10.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-109) Howard left the Magic as their all-time leading scorer, shot blocker, and rebounder.

#### 2012–2017: Rob Hennigan era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Orlando_Magic&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2012–2017: Rob Hennigan era")]

[![Image 31](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Nikola_Vucevic_Dec_2013_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Nikola_Vucevic_Dec_2013_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nikola_Vucevic_Dec_2013_(cropped).jpg)

[Nikola Vučević](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Vu%C4%8Devi%C4%87 "Nikola Vučević") playing for the Magic

Following the trade of Dwight Howard, the Magic entered into a state of rebuilding with [Maurice Harkless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Harkless "Maurice Harkless") and [Nikola Vučević](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Vu%C4%8Devi%C4%87 "Nikola Vučević"). On August 29, the Magic signed free agent guard [E'Twaun Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E'Twaun_Moore "E'Twaun Moore"). On December 2, 2012, Howard's first game against his former team, the Magic defeated the Lakers 113–103.

On February 21, 2013, the Magic traded [JJ Redick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JJ_Redick "JJ Redick"), [Ish Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ish_Smith "Ish Smith") and [Gustavo Ayón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustavo_Ay%C3%B3n "Gustavo Ayón") to the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks"). In return, the Magic received [Beno Udrih](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beno_Udrih "Beno Udrih"), [Tobias Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tobias_Harris "Tobias Harris") and rookie [Doron Lamb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doron_Lamb "Doron Lamb"). The Magic also traded [Josh McRoberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_McRoberts "Josh McRoberts") to the [Charlotte Bobcats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Bobcats "Charlotte Bobcats") for [Hakim Warrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hakim_Warrick "Hakim Warrick") who was waived 2 days later. The Magic finish the 2012–13 season 20–62 as the worst record in the NBA, missing the playoffs for the first time since 2006.

On June 27, 2013, the Orlando Magic had the second pick in the first round of the [2013 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NBA_draft "2013 NBA draft"). The Magic used their [lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") pick to draft [Big Ten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten "Big Ten") Defensive Player of the Year,[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-110) shooting guard [Victor Oladipo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Oladipo "Victor Oladipo") from [Indiana University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_University_Bloomington "Indiana University Bloomington"). The Magic also had the 51st pick in the second round of the NBA draft. They used this pick to draft forward [Romero Osby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romero_Osby "Romero Osby") from the [University of Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oklahoma "University of Oklahoma"). Osby averaged 16 points, seven rebounds, and 1.3 assists during his senior NCAA season at Oklahoma but was cut by the Magic before the season opener.

The Magic finished the 2013–14 season with a 23–59 record, third worst in the NBA. The draft lottery gave them the fourth pick in the [2014 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NBA_draft "2014 NBA draft"). In the draft, they selected [Aaron Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Gordon "Aaron Gordon") with the fourth pick and [Dario Šarić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dario_%C5%A0ari%C4%87 "Dario Šarić") with the 12th pick. Saric was then swapped for the 10th pick, [Elfrid Payton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elfrid_Payton_(basketball) "Elfrid Payton (basketball)") in exchange for a 2017 first round pick and a future second round pick. [Roy Devyn Marble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Devyn_Marble "Roy Devyn Marble") was selected with the 56th pick in the second round. On February 5, 2015, Jacque Vaughn was relieved of his head coaching duties after coaching 2+1⁄2 seasons for the Magic. His overall record was 58–158. He was replaced by interim head coach [James Borrego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Borrego "James Borrego").

On May 29, 2015, the Magic hired their former point guard [Scott Skiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Skiles "Scott Skiles") as the franchise's 12th head coach.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-112)

On June 25, 2015, in the [2015 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft "2015 NBA draft"), Orlando selected [Mario Hezonja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Hezonja "Mario Hezonja") with the fifth overall pick and [Tyler Harvey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyler_Harvey_(basketball) "Tyler Harvey (basketball)") with the 51st overall pick.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-113) On February 16, 2016, the Magic traded [Tobias Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tobias_Harris "Tobias Harris") to the [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons") in exchange for [Ersan İlyasova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ersan_%C4%B0lyasova "Ersan İlyasova") and [Brandon Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Jennings "Brandon Jennings").[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-114)

On May 12, 2016, Skiles stepped down as head coach of the Orlando Magic.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-115) On May 19, the Orlando Magic agreed to a deal with former Indiana Pacers coach [Frank Vogel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Vogel "Frank Vogel") to become the next head coach of the team.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-116)

With Vogel as their new coach, the Magic made many changes to their roster during the off-season. On June 23, 2016, in the [2016 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft "2016 NBA draft") the Magic selected [Domantas Sabonis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domantas_Sabonis "Domantas Sabonis") 11th overall, but then traded Sabonis and shooting guard [Victor Oladipo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Oladipo "Victor Oladipo") for defensive power forward [Serge Ibaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serge_Ibaka "Serge Ibaka") of the [Oklahoma City Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City_Thunder "Oklahoma City Thunder"). During free agency the Magic re-signed [Evan Fournier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Fournier "Evan Fournier") to a five-year, $85 million contract and also signed [Bismack Biyombo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bismack_Biyombo "Bismack Biyombo"), [Jeff Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Green_(basketball) "Jeff Green (basketball)"), and [D. J. Augustin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._J._Augustin "D. J. Augustin"). On July 15, [C. J. Wilcox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Wilcox "C. J. Wilcox") was acquired, along with cash considerations, from the Clippers in exchange for [Devyn Marble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devyn_Marble "Devyn Marble") and a future second round draft pick.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-re-sign-117)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-119)

On February 14, 2017, Ibaka was traded to the [Toronto Raptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Raptors "Toronto Raptors") in exchange for [Terrence Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrence_Ross "Terrence Ross") and a future first-round draft pick.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-120) The Magic finished the 2016–17 season with the third worst record in their conference, finishing 29–53.

#### 2017–2022: Jeff Weltman era

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Orlando_Magic&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2017–2022: Jeff Weltman era")]

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/72/Markelle_Fultz_%2850639064136%29.jpg/250px-Markelle_Fultz_%2850639064136%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Markelle_Fultz_(50639064136).jpg)

[Markelle Fultz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markelle_Fultz "Markelle Fultz") playing for the Magic

In the summer of 2017, the Magic made various changes, the first being the firing of general manager Rob Hennigan on April 13. On May 23, the Magic named Jeff Weltman, the former general manager of the Toronto Raptors, as president of basketball operations and named John Hammond, the former general manager for the Milwaukee Bucks, as the new general manager. With the sixth overall pick in the [2017 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_NBA_draft "2017 NBA draft"), Orlando drafted Florida State forward, [Jonathan Isaac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Isaac "Jonathan Isaac"). During free agency the Magic signed [Jonathon Simmons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathon_Simmons "Jonathon Simmons"), [Arron Afflalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arron_Afflalo "Arron Afflalo"), [Shelvin Mack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shelvin_Mack "Shelvin Mack"), [Marreese Speights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marreese_Speights "Marreese Speights"), [Khem Birch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khem_Birch "Khem Birch") and [Adreian Payne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adreian_Payne "Adreian Payne").

On October 6, 2017, the Magic announced that former superstar [Tracy McGrady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_McGrady "Tracy McGrady"), had rejoined the team as assistant to the CEO.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-121)

On February 8, 2018, the Magic traded starting point guard [Elfrid Payton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elfrid_Payton_(basketball) "Elfrid Payton (basketball)") to the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") in exchange for a 2018 second-round pick.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-122)

On April 12, 2018, head coach Frank Vogel was fired by the Magic after the conclusion of the 2017–18 regular season.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-123) On May 30, the Magic named [Steve Clifford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Clifford "Steve Clifford") as their new head coach.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic#cite_note-124)

While the Magic won the opening game, Milwaukee won the next four ending the Magic's season in round one for the second year in a row.
