"**Local Ad**" is the ninth episode of the [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Office_(American_TV_series)_season_4 "The Office (American TV series) season 4") of the American [comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy "Comedy")[television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_program "Television program")_[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Office (American TV series)")_ and the show's sixty-second episode overall. The episode was written by [B. J. Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Novak "B. J. Novak"), who also acts in the show as [Ryan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Howard_(The_Office) "Ryan Howard (The Office)"), and directed by [Jason Reitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Reitman "Jason Reitman"). It originally aired in the United States on October 25, 2007, on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-Spider-1)

After a video team is brought to the office to create a commercial for the company, Michael decides that the employees of the Scranton branch of Dunder Mifflin can create a better commercial. While the majority of the staff work on the commercial, Dwight, still depressed from his break-up with Angela, instead chooses to play a computer game.

## Plot

When [Michael Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Scott_(The_Office) "Michael Scott (The Office)") learns that the [Scranton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scranton,_Pennsylvania "Scranton, Pennsylvania") branch's participation in a [Dunder Mifflin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunder_Mifflin "Dunder Mifflin") television commercial is limited to five seconds of the staff waving at the camera, he dismisses the advertising consultants sent to the branch, and convinces the company's corporate headquarters to consider an alternative version that he will produce himself.

Michael asks [Pam Beesly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pam_Beesly "Pam Beesly") to design an animated logo, and she works all night on it.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-CB-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3)[Phyllis Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyllis_Vance "Phyllis Vance")'s mission to enlist visiting author [Sue Grafton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sue_Grafton "Sue Grafton") to appear in the ad is unsuccessful. Headed by [Darryl Philbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darryl_Philbin "Darryl Philbin"), a group of employees write and perform a [jingle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jingle "Jingle") for the commercial, which Michael ultimately rejects. [Andy Bernard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Bernard "Andy Bernard"), meanwhile, struggles throughout the day to recall the [product name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_name "Product name") from an advertising jingle that contains the lyrics "Gimme a break. Gimme a break. Break me off a piece of that..."

[Dwight Schrute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Schrute "Dwight Schrute"), playing in the online virtual world of _[Second Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second\_Life "Second Life")_, has created an [avatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar_(computing) "Avatar (computing)") named Dwight Shelford, also a paper salesman, patterned after his once-perfect real life. He now uses _Second Life_ as an escape from his real-life troubles, even creating a virtual _Second Life_, called _Second Second Life_. [Jim Halpert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Halpert "Jim Halpert") creates his own avatar named Jim Samtanko, a guitar-playing [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") sportswriter, and enters _Second Life_ in order to spy on Dwight.

Dwight reluctantly becomes Andy's confidante regarding his relationship with [Angela Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Martin "Angela Martin"), Dwight's former girlfriend. Dwight's spirits are lifted when he learns that, during a [makeout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Making_out "Making out") session with Andy, Angela cried, "Oh, D!". Andy assumes "D" is a diminutive for Andy.

After the corporate headquarters rejects Michael's ad, the office employees gather at Poor Richard's Pub to watch the professionally filmed commercial, which Michael refers to as "the world premiere of corporate crapfest." After the commercial, Jim plays Michael's version of the ad on the bar's television set. Over the theme from _[Chariots of Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chariots\_of\_Fire\_(instrumental) "Chariots of Fire (instrumental)")_, as Michael narrates trite catchphrases,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3) a sheet of paper is depicted making a journey around the world, carrying a variety of messages meaningful to the recipients; Pam's animated whirling sheets of paper coalesce into the company logo to end the ad. The employees as well as the other patrons of the bar show their approval.

Andy, still trying to recall the product name from the jingle on the basis that it has to rhyme, incorrectly concludes that it promotes [Fancy Feast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fancy_Feast "Fancy Feast") cat food.

## Production

"Local Ad" was the seventh episode of the series written by [B. J. Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Novak "B. J. Novak"), who also acts in the show as [Ryan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Howard_(The_Office) "Ryan Howard (The Office)"), and the first episode of the series directed by [Jason Reitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Reitman "Jason Reitman"), who directed the films _[Juno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno\_(film) "Juno (film)")_ and _[Thank You for Smoking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank\_You\_for\_Smoking "Thank You for Smoking")_. When speaking about his directorial experience with _The Office_, Reitman stated that "Anyhow, the whole experience was awesome. They're all geniuses over there. I didn’t have to contribute much at the end of the day because they're all so on their game." He also stated that "Weird moment of production design surprise – There's a three ring binder on [Creed's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creed_Bratton "Creed Bratton") desk with the logo from the Academy of Tobacco Studies that we created for [_Thank You For_] _Smoking_. I have no idea how it got there and neither does he."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-4) B.J. Novak's brother [Jesse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Novak "Jesse Novak"), a musician, contributed by writing the second commercial jingle in the episode, and the third jingle was written by [Craig Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Robinson_(actor) "Craig Robinson (actor)"), the actor who plays reoccurring character [Darryl Philbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darryl_Philbin "Darryl Philbin") and leads the cast members in performing both the second and third jingle.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-commentary-5)

The _[Second Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second\_Life "Second Life")_ scenes in "Local Ad" were produced by Clear Ink of Berkeley, CA, using existing locations within _Second Life_ as well as virtual sets created for the episode.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-8) In a study made by IAG Research, the appearance of _Second Life_ in "Local Ad" was rated eighth in the top ten most effective product placements of 2007. _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Office (American TV series)")_ was the only non-[reality show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reality_television "Reality television") to make the list, and _Second Life_ was the only product on the list that did not pay for its placement.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-9)

The two sides of Michael and Ryan's phone conversation were filmed simultaneously, with a [second unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_unit "Second unit") shooting Ryan's part.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-commentary-5)

Scenes which were filmed for the episode but deleted include Toby suggesting the ad be filmed in slow-motion, Jim and Michael roleplaying as a producer and an artistically idealistic director, and Jim encasing Dwight's rocket launcher in gelatin in _Second Life_.

## Reception

"Local Ad" received a 5.2 [Nielsen rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_rating "Nielsen rating") and an 8% Share. The episode was watched by an estimate audience of 8.98 million viewers and achieved a 4.7/11 in the key adults 18–49 demographic. This means that 4.1 percent of all people aged 18–49 viewed the episode, and eleven percent of all people watching television at the time viewed the episode.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-10)

"Local Ad" received generally favorable reviews from critics. Travis Fickett of _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ gave the episode a favorable review, saying "This episode is a prime example of how _The Office_ is able to do broad comedy while at the same time treating its characters as real people." Fickett went on to praise the acting of [Rainn Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainn_Wilson "Rainn Wilson") as a depressed Dwight, as well as the story's twist. Fickett stated that "A great twist here is that we think we're watching Michael pilot a sinking ship as usual, but in fact – the ad is quite good. There's some clever stuff in there, albeit some of it not exactly professional in its production, but Michael doesn't do such a bad job."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-11) Like Fickett, Christine Fenno of _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ gave the episode a favorable review. Fenno said that "The premise of this episode, 'Local Ad' — the Scranton staffers shoot a commercial — was strong, and allowed almost every ensemble member to shine." Fenno also praised the acting work of [Ed Helms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Helms "Ed Helms") as Andy, as well as [Steve Carell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Carell "Steve Carell") as Michael.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-12) Oscar Dahl, a senior writer for [BuddyTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BuddyTV "BuddyTV"), praised the episode, but also felt that its thirty-minute length created a stark contrast to the previous four episodes' hour-long run, saying "tonight's episode felt short. Really short."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-13)

For his work on this episode, [B. J. Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Novak "B. J. Novak") was nominated for a [Writers Guild of America Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America_Award "Writers Guild of America Award") for [Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America_Award_for_Best_Screenplay_%E2%80%93_Episodic_Comedy "Writers Guild of America Award for Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy"), but lost to another episode of _The Office_, "[The Job](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Job_(The_Office) "The Job (The Office)")."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-14)

"**Local Ad**" is the ninth episode of the [fourth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Office_(American_TV_series)_season_4 "The Office (American TV series) season 4") of the American [comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy "Comedy")[television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_program "Television program")_[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Office (American TV series)")_ and the show's sixty-second episode overall. The episode was written by [B. J. Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Novak "B. J. Novak"), who also acts in the show as [Ryan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Howard_(The_Office) "Ryan Howard (The Office)"), and directed by [Jason Reitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Reitman "Jason Reitman"). It originally aired in the United States on October 25, 2007, on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-Spider-1)

After a video team is brought to the office to create a commercial for the company, Michael decides that the employees of the Scranton branch of Dunder Mifflin can create a better commercial. While the majority of the staff work on the commercial, Dwight, still depressed from his break-up with Angela, instead chooses to play a computer game.

## Plot

When [Michael Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Scott_(The_Office) "Michael Scott (The Office)") learns that the [Scranton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scranton,_Pennsylvania "Scranton, Pennsylvania") branch's participation in a [Dunder Mifflin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunder_Mifflin "Dunder Mifflin") television commercial is limited to five seconds of the staff waving at the camera, he dismisses the advertising consultants sent to the branch, and convinces the company's corporate headquarters to consider an alternative version that he will produce himself.

Michael asks [Pam Beesly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pam_Beesly "Pam Beesly") to design an animated logo, and she works all night on it.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-CB-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3)[Phyllis Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyllis_Vance "Phyllis Vance")'s mission to enlist visiting author [Sue Grafton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sue_Grafton "Sue Grafton") to appear in the ad is unsuccessful. Headed by [Darryl Philbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darryl_Philbin "Darryl Philbin"), a group of employees write and perform a [jingle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jingle "Jingle") for the commercial, which Michael ultimately rejects. [Andy Bernard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Bernard "Andy Bernard"), meanwhile, struggles throughout the day to recall the [product name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_name "Product name") from an advertising jingle that contains the lyrics "Gimme a break. Gimme a break. Break me off a piece of that..."

[Dwight Schrute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Schrute "Dwight Schrute"), playing in the online virtual world of _[Second Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second\_Life "Second Life")_, has created an [avatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar_(computing) "Avatar (computing)") named Dwight Shelford, also a paper salesman, patterned after his once-perfect real life. He now uses _Second Life_ as an escape from his real-life troubles, even creating a virtual _Second Life_, called _Second Second Life_. [Jim Halpert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Halpert "Jim Halpert") creates his own avatar named Jim Samtanko, a guitar-playing [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") sportswriter, and enters _Second Life_ in order to spy on Dwight.

Dwight reluctantly becomes Andy's confidante regarding his relationship with [Angela Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Martin "Angela Martin"), Dwight's former girlfriend. Dwight's spirits are lifted when he learns that, during a [makeout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Making_out "Making out") session with Andy, Angela cried, "Oh, D!". Andy assumes "D" is a diminutive for Andy.

After the corporate headquarters rejects Michael's ad, the office employees gather at Poor Richard's Pub to watch the professionally filmed commercial, which Michael refers to as "the world premiere of corporate crapfest." After the commercial, Jim plays Michael's version of the ad on the bar's television set. Over the theme from _[Chariots of Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chariots\_of\_Fire\_(instrumental) "Chariots of Fire (instrumental)")_, as Michael narrates trite catchphrases,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3) a sheet of paper is depicted making a journey around the world, carrying a variety of messages meaningful to the recipients; Pam's animated whirling sheets of paper coalesce into the company logo to end the ad. The employees as well as the other patrons of the bar show their approval.

Andy, still trying to recall the product name from the jingle on the basis that it has to rhyme, incorrectly concludes that it promotes [Fancy Feast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fancy_Feast "Fancy Feast") cat food.

## Production

"Local Ad" was the seventh episode of the series written by [B. J. Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Novak "B. J. Novak"), who also acts in the show as [Ryan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Howard_(The_Office) "Ryan Howard (The Office)"), and the first episode of the series directed by [Jason Reitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Reitman "Jason Reitman"), who directed the films _[Juno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno\_(film) "Juno (film)")_ and _[Thank You for Smoking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank\_You\_for\_Smoking "Thank You for Smoking")_. When speaking about his directorial experience with _The Office_, Reitman stated that "Anyhow, the whole experience was awesome. They're all geniuses over there. I didn’t have to contribute much at the end of the day because they're all so on their game." He also stated that "Weird moment of production design surprise – There's a three ring binder on [Creed's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creed_Bratton "Creed Bratton") desk with the logo from the Academy of Tobacco Studies that we created for [_Thank You For_] _Smoking_. I have no idea how it got there and neither does he."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-4) B.J. Novak's brother [Jesse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Novak "Jesse Novak"), a musician, contributed by writing the second commercial jingle in the episode, and the third jingle was written by [Craig Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Robinson_(actor) "Craig Robinson (actor)"), the actor who plays reoccurring character [Darryl Philbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darryl_Philbin "Darryl Philbin") and leads the cast members in performing both the second and third jingle.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-commentary-5)

The _[Second Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second\_Life "Second Life")_ scenes in "Local Ad" were produced by Clear Ink of Berkeley, CA, using existing locations within _Second Life_ as well as virtual sets created for the episode.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-8) In a study made by IAG Research, the appearance of _Second Life_ in "Local Ad" was rated eighth in the top ten most effective product placements of 2007. _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(American\_TV\_series) "The Office (American TV series)")_ was the only non-[reality show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reality_television "Reality television") to make the list, and _Second Life_ was the only product on the list that did not pay for its placement.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-9)

The two sides of Michael and Ryan's phone conversation were filmed simultaneously, with a [second unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_unit "Second unit") shooting Ryan's part.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-commentary-5)

Scenes which were filmed for the episode but deleted include Toby suggesting the ad be filmed in slow-motion, Jim and Michael roleplaying as a producer and an artistically idealistic director, and Jim encasing Dwight's rocket launcher in gelatin in _Second Life_.

## Reception

"Local Ad" received a 5.2 [Nielsen rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_rating "Nielsen rating") and an 8% Share. The episode was watched by an estimate audience of 8.98 million viewers and achieved a 4.7/11 in the key adults 18–49 demographic. This means that 4.1 percent of all people aged 18–49 viewed the episode, and eleven percent of all people watching television at the time viewed the episode.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-10)

"Local Ad" received generally favorable reviews from critics. Travis Fickett of _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ gave the episode a favorable review, saying "This episode is a prime example of how _The Office_ is able to do broad comedy while at the same time treating its characters as real people." Fickett went on to praise the acting of [Rainn Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainn_Wilson "Rainn Wilson") as a depressed Dwight, as well as the story's twist. Fickett stated that "A great twist here is that we think we're watching Michael pilot a sinking ship as usual, but in fact – the ad is quite good. There's some clever stuff in there, albeit some of it not exactly professional in its production, but Michael doesn't do such a bad job."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-11) Like Fickett, Christine Fenno of _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ gave the episode a favorable review. Fenno said that "The premise of this episode, 'Local Ad' — the Scranton staffers shoot a commercial — was strong, and allowed almost every ensemble member to shine." Fenno also praised the acting work of [Ed Helms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Helms "Ed Helms") as Andy, as well as [Steve Carell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Carell "Steve Carell") as Michael.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-12) Oscar Dahl, a senior writer for [BuddyTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BuddyTV "BuddyTV"), praised the episode, but also felt that its thirty-minute length created a stark contrast to the previous four episodes' hour-long run, saying "tonight's episode felt short. Really short."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-13)

For his work on this episode, [B. J. Novak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._J._Novak "B. J. Novak") was nominated for a [Writers Guild of America Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America_Award "Writers Guild of America Award") for [Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writers_Guild_of_America_Award_for_Best_Screenplay_%E2%80%93_Episodic_Comedy "Writers Guild of America Award for Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy"), but lost to another episode of _The Office_, "[The Job](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Job_(The_Office) "The Job (The Office)")."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-14)

**Pamela Ann Melroy** (born September 17, 1961) is an American retired [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force") officer and [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")[astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut") who also served as the [deputy administrator of NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Administrator_of_NASA "Deputy Administrator of NASA"). She served as pilot on [Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle") missions [STS-92](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-92 "STS-92") and [STS-112](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-112 "STS-112") and commanded mission STS-120 before leaving the agency in August 2009. After serving as deputy program manager of Space Exploration Initiatives with [Lockheed Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Martin "Lockheed Martin"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-1) Melroy joined the [Federal Aviation Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Aviation_Administration "Federal Aviation Administration") in 2011, where she was a senior technical advisor and director of field operations for the FAA's Office of Commercial Space Transportation.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-2)

In 2013, she left the FAA and joined [DARPA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA "DARPA") as deputy director of the Tactical Technology Office. She left the agency in February 2017.

In November 2021, Melroy was inducted into the [United States Astronaut Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Astronaut_Hall_of_Fame "United States Astronaut Hall of Fame") at the [Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center_Visitor_Complex "Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex"). The ceremony, originally planned for May 2020, was delayed due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-4)

Melroy served as [Deputy Administrator of NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Administrator_of_NASA "Deputy Administrator of NASA") from 2021 to 2025[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-6), helping design strategies like Moon to Mars ([Artemis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artemis_program "Artemis program")), NASA 2040, Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Commercialization and Space Sustainability[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-7).

Today, she works as a strategic advisor and keynote speaker[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-8).

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Melroy was born in [Palo Alto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palo_Alto "Palo Alto"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), and graduated from [Bishop Kearney High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop_Kearney_High_School_(Irondequoit,_New_York) "Bishop Kearney High School (Irondequoit, New York)") in [Rochester, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochester,_New_York "Rochester, New York") in 1979.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-9) She received a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") in [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics "Physics") and [astronomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronomy "Astronomy") from [Wellesley College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellesley_College "Wellesley College") in 1983.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-Wellesley-10) She then earned her [Master of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Science "Master of Science") in [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_science "Earth science") and [planetary science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetary_science "Planetary science") from the [Massachusetts Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Institute_of_Technology "Massachusetts Institute of Technology") in 1984. On May 18, 2008, Melroy received an honorary degree from [Iona College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iona_College_(New_York) "Iona College (New York)") in [New Rochelle, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Rochelle,_New_York "New Rochelle, New York").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Military

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Military")]

Melroy was commissioned through [Air Force ROTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_ROTC "Air Force ROTC"), Detachment 365, in 1984. After completing a master's degree, she attended Undergraduate Pilot Training at [Reese Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reese_Air_Force_Base "Reese Air Force Base") in Lubbock, Texas and was graduated in 1985. She flew the [KC-10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonnell_Douglas_KC-10_Extender "McDonnell Douglas KC-10 Extender") for six years at [Barksdale Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barksdale_Air_Force_Base "Barksdale Air Force Base") in Bossier City, Louisiana, as a copilot, aircraft commander and instructor pilot. Melroy is a veteran of [the United States invasion of Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Just_Cause "Operation Just Cause") and Operation [Desert Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert_Shield "Desert Shield")/[Desert Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert_Storm "Desert Storm"), with over 200 combat and combat support hours. In June 1991, she attended the Air Force Test Pilot School at [Edwards Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwards_Air_Force_Base "Edwards Air Force Base"), California. Upon her graduation, she was assigned to the [C-17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_C-17_Globemaster_III "Boeing C-17 Globemaster III") Combined Test Force, where she served as a test pilot until her selection for the astronaut program. She has logged over 5,000 hours of flight time in over 50 different aircraft. Melroy retired from the Air Force in February 2007.

### NASA

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: NASA")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Sts112-314-029.jpg/250px-Sts112-314-029.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sts112-314-029.jpg)

Melroy aboard the ISS during [STS-112](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-112 "STS-112")

Selected as an astronaut candidate by [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") in December 1994, Melroy reported to the [Johnson Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_Space_Center "Johnson Space Center") in March 1995. She completed a year of training and evaluation and was qualified for flight assignment as a shuttle pilot. Initially assigned to astronaut support duties for launch and landing, she also worked Advanced Projects for the Astronaut Office. She also performed CAPCOM duties in mission control. Melroy served on the _Columbia_ Reconstruction Team as the lead for the crew module and served as deputy project manager for the _Columbia_ crew survival investigation team. In her final position, she served as branch chief for the Orion branch of the Astronaut Office.

Melroy served as pilot on two flights (STS-92 in 2000 and STS-112 in 2002), and was the mission commander on STS-120 in 2007, making her the second woman to command a Space Shuttle mission (after [Eileen Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eileen_Collins "Eileen Collins")).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-11) The STS-120 crew visited the station during [Expedition 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_16 "Expedition 16"), commanded by [Peggy Whitson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peggy_Whitson "Peggy Whitson"). Whitson was the first female ISS commander, making the STS-120 mission the first time that two female mission commanders were in orbit at the same time.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-bionasa-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-13)

She has logged more than 924 hours (over 38 days) in space.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-bionasa-12)

#### Spaceflight experience

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Spaceflight experience")]

*   [STS-92](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-92 "STS-92")_[Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery")_ (October 11–24, 2000) was launched from the [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center"), Florida and returned to land at Edwards Air Force Base, California. During the 13-day flight, the seven member crew attached the [Z1 Truss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z1_Truss "Z1 Truss") and Pressurized Mating Adapter 3 to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") using _Discovery_'s robotic arm and performed four spacewalks to configure these elements. This expansion of the ISS opened the door for future assembly missions and prepared the station for its first resident crew. The STS-92 mission was accomplished in 202 orbits, traveling 5.3 million miles in 12 days, 21 hours, 40 minutes and 25 seconds.

*   [STS-112](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-112 "STS-112")_[Atlantis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Atlantis "Space Shuttle Atlantis")_ (October 7–18, 2002) launched from and returned to land at the Kennedy Space Center, Florida. STS-112 was an International Space Station assembly mission during which the crew conducted joint operations with the Expedition-5 by delivering and installing the [S1 Truss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S1_Truss "S1 Truss") (the third piece of the station's 11-piece Integrated Truss Structure). It took three spacewalks to outfit and activate the new component, during which Melroy acted as internal spacewalk choreographer. STS-112 was the first shuttle mission to use a camera on the External Tank, providing a live view of the launch to flight controllers and NASA TV viewers. The mission was accomplished in 170 orbits, traveling 4.5 million miles in 10 days, 19 hours, and 58 minutes.

*   STS-120_[Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery")_ (October 23 – November 7, 2007) launched from and returned to land at the Kennedy Space Center.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-:0-14) During the mission, the [Node 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node_2 "Node 2") element named _Harmony_ was delivered to the International Space Station. This element opened up the capability for future international laboratories to be added to the station. In addition, the P6 Solar Array was re-located from the Z1 Truss to the end of the port side of the Integrated Truss Structure. During the re-deploy of the array, the array panels snagged and were damaged. An unplanned spacewalk was successfully performed to repair the array. The mission was accomplished in 238 orbits, traveling 6.2 million miles in 15 days, 2 hours, and 23 minutes.

#### Deputy administrator

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Deputy administrator")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Pam_Melroy_in_2022.jpg/250px-Pam_Melroy_in_2022.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pam_Melroy_in_2022.jpg)

Pam Melroy in 2022

In November 2020, Melroy was announced as a member of [President-elect Joe Biden's presidential transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_transition_of_Joe_Biden "Presidential transition of Joe Biden") Agency Review Team, where her role was to support transition efforts related to NASA. This fueled speculation that Melroy was under consideration for the role of [NASA Administrator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrator_of_NASA "Administrator of NASA") in the [Biden administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biden_administration "Biden administration") (then-Administrator [James Bridenstine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Bridenstine "James Bridenstine") had indicated that he did not intend to stay in the role under Biden, even if asked).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-16)

On April 16, 2021, the White House announced their intent to nominate Melroy to be NASA's deputy administrator, under former Democratic Senator [Bill Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Nelson "Bill Nelson"), who was nominated by the White House on March 19, 2021, to be the agency's administrator.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-17) On April 22, 2021, her nomination was sent to the Senate.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-18) The [Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Commerce,_Science,_and_Transportation "United States Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation") held a hearing on May 20, 2021, in which Melroy won strong bipartisan support to be deputy administrator. During her hearing, Melroy expressed support for extending the lifetime of the International Space Station, and said she would work closely with Nelson in running the agency.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-19)

On June 16, 2021, Melroy's nomination was reported out of the [Senate Commerce Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_Commerce_Committee "Senate Commerce Committee") by voice vote and the following day, she was confirmed by the full [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") with [unanimous consent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unanimous_consent "Unanimous consent").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-20) On June 21, 2021, Melroy was sworn into office by administrator [Bill Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Nelson "Bill Nelson").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-21) Melroy served as NASA deputy administrator through the end of the [Biden Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biden_Administration "Biden Administration"), leaving office January 20, 2025. On April 25, 2025, Melroy was honored with the National Space Trophy by the Rotary National Award for Space Achievement Foundation,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-22) and in September 2025, it was announced that Melroy was appointed to the Board of Directors for Venus Aerospace.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-23)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Melroy is married to Douglas Hollett, a geologist, who was previously acting [assistant secretary for fossil energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_Secretary_for_Fossil_Energy "Assistant Secretary for Fossil Energy") in the [United States Department of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Energy "United States Department of Energy") and vice president for Southeast Asia exploration at [Marathon Oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_Oil "Marathon Oil").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-:0-14)

**Pamela Ann Melroy** (born September 17, 1961) is an American retired [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force") officer and [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")[astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut") who also served as the [deputy administrator of NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Administrator_of_NASA "Deputy Administrator of NASA"). She served as pilot on [Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle") missions [STS-92](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-92 "STS-92") and [STS-112](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-112 "STS-112") and commanded mission STS-120 before leaving the agency in August 2009. After serving as deputy program manager of Space Exploration Initiatives with [Lockheed Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Martin "Lockheed Martin"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-1) Melroy joined the [Federal Aviation Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Aviation_Administration "Federal Aviation Administration") in 2011, where she was a senior technical advisor and director of field operations for the FAA's Office of Commercial Space Transportation.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-2)

In 2013, she left the FAA and joined [DARPA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA "DARPA") as deputy director of the Tactical Technology Office. She left the agency in February 2017.

In November 2021, Melroy was inducted into the [United States Astronaut Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Astronaut_Hall_of_Fame "United States Astronaut Hall of Fame") at the [Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center_Visitor_Complex "Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex"). The ceremony, originally planned for May 2020, was delayed due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-4)

Melroy served as [Deputy Administrator of NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Administrator_of_NASA "Deputy Administrator of NASA") from 2021 to 2025[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-6), helping design strategies like Moon to Mars ([Artemis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artemis_program "Artemis program")), NASA 2040, Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Commercialization and Space Sustainability[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-7).

Today, she works as a strategic advisor and keynote speaker[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-8).

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Melroy was born in [Palo Alto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palo_Alto "Palo Alto"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), and graduated from [Bishop Kearney High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop_Kearney_High_School_(Irondequoit,_New_York) "Bishop Kearney High School (Irondequoit, New York)") in [Rochester, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochester,_New_York "Rochester, New York") in 1979.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-9) She received a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") in [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics "Physics") and [astronomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronomy "Astronomy") from [Wellesley College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wellesley_College "Wellesley College") in 1983.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-Wellesley-10) She then earned her [Master of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Science "Master of Science") in [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_science "Earth science") and [planetary science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetary_science "Planetary science") from the [Massachusetts Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Institute_of_Technology "Massachusetts Institute of Technology") in 1984. On May 18, 2008, Melroy received an honorary degree from [Iona College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iona_College_(New_York) "Iona College (New York)") in [New Rochelle, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Rochelle,_New_York "New Rochelle, New York").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Military

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Military")]

Melroy was commissioned through [Air Force ROTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_ROTC "Air Force ROTC"), Detachment 365, in 1984. After completing a master's degree, she attended Undergraduate Pilot Training at [Reese Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reese_Air_Force_Base "Reese Air Force Base") in Lubbock, Texas and was graduated in 1985. She flew the [KC-10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonnell_Douglas_KC-10_Extender "McDonnell Douglas KC-10 Extender") for six years at [Barksdale Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barksdale_Air_Force_Base "Barksdale Air Force Base") in Bossier City, Louisiana, as a copilot, aircraft commander and instructor pilot. Melroy is a veteran of [the United States invasion of Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Just_Cause "Operation Just Cause") and Operation [Desert Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert_Shield "Desert Shield")/[Desert Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert_Storm "Desert Storm"), with over 200 combat and combat support hours. In June 1991, she attended the Air Force Test Pilot School at [Edwards Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwards_Air_Force_Base "Edwards Air Force Base"), California. Upon her graduation, she was assigned to the [C-17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_C-17_Globemaster_III "Boeing C-17 Globemaster III") Combined Test Force, where she served as a test pilot until her selection for the astronaut program. She has logged over 5,000 hours of flight time in over 50 different aircraft. Melroy retired from the Air Force in February 2007.

### NASA

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: NASA")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Sts112-314-029.jpg/250px-Sts112-314-029.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sts112-314-029.jpg)

Melroy aboard the ISS during [STS-112](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-112 "STS-112")

Selected as an astronaut candidate by [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") in December 1994, Melroy reported to the [Johnson Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_Space_Center "Johnson Space Center") in March 1995. She completed a year of training and evaluation and was qualified for flight assignment as a shuttle pilot. Initially assigned to astronaut support duties for launch and landing, she also worked Advanced Projects for the Astronaut Office. She also performed CAPCOM duties in mission control. Melroy served on the _Columbia_ Reconstruction Team as the lead for the crew module and served as deputy project manager for the _Columbia_ crew survival investigation team. In her final position, she served as branch chief for the Orion branch of the Astronaut Office.

Melroy served as pilot on two flights (STS-92 in 2000 and STS-112 in 2002), and was the mission commander on STS-120 in 2007, making her the second woman to command a Space Shuttle mission (after [Eileen Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eileen_Collins "Eileen Collins")).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-11) The STS-120 crew visited the station during [Expedition 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expedition_16 "Expedition 16"), commanded by [Peggy Whitson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peggy_Whitson "Peggy Whitson"). Whitson was the first female ISS commander, making the STS-120 mission the first time that two female mission commanders were in orbit at the same time.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-bionasa-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-13)

She has logged more than 924 hours (over 38 days) in space.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-bionasa-12)

#### Spaceflight experience

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Spaceflight experience")]

*   [STS-92](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-92 "STS-92")_[Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery")_ (October 11–24, 2000) was launched from the [Kennedy Space Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Space_Center "Kennedy Space Center"), Florida and returned to land at Edwards Air Force Base, California. During the 13-day flight, the seven member crew attached the [Z1 Truss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z1_Truss "Z1 Truss") and Pressurized Mating Adapter 3 to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") using _Discovery_'s robotic arm and performed four spacewalks to configure these elements. This expansion of the ISS opened the door for future assembly missions and prepared the station for its first resident crew. The STS-92 mission was accomplished in 202 orbits, traveling 5.3 million miles in 12 days, 21 hours, 40 minutes and 25 seconds.

*   [STS-112](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-112 "STS-112")_[Atlantis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Atlantis "Space Shuttle Atlantis")_ (October 7–18, 2002) launched from and returned to land at the Kennedy Space Center, Florida. STS-112 was an International Space Station assembly mission during which the crew conducted joint operations with the Expedition-5 by delivering and installing the [S1 Truss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S1_Truss "S1 Truss") (the third piece of the station's 11-piece Integrated Truss Structure). It took three spacewalks to outfit and activate the new component, during which Melroy acted as internal spacewalk choreographer. STS-112 was the first shuttle mission to use a camera on the External Tank, providing a live view of the launch to flight controllers and NASA TV viewers. The mission was accomplished in 170 orbits, traveling 4.5 million miles in 10 days, 19 hours, and 58 minutes.

*   STS-120_[Discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space\_Shuttle\_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery")_ (October 23 – November 7, 2007) launched from and returned to land at the Kennedy Space Center.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-:0-14) During the mission, the [Node 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node_2 "Node 2") element named _Harmony_ was delivered to the International Space Station. This element opened up the capability for future international laboratories to be added to the station. In addition, the P6 Solar Array was re-located from the Z1 Truss to the end of the port side of the Integrated Truss Structure. During the re-deploy of the array, the array panels snagged and were damaged. An unplanned spacewalk was successfully performed to repair the array. The mission was accomplished in 238 orbits, traveling 6.2 million miles in 15 days, 2 hours, and 23 minutes.

#### Deputy administrator

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Deputy administrator")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Pam_Melroy_in_2022.jpg/250px-Pam_Melroy_in_2022.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pam_Melroy_in_2022.jpg)

Pam Melroy in 2022

In November 2020, Melroy was announced as a member of [President-elect Joe Biden's presidential transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_transition_of_Joe_Biden "Presidential transition of Joe Biden") Agency Review Team, where her role was to support transition efforts related to NASA. This fueled speculation that Melroy was under consideration for the role of [NASA Administrator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrator_of_NASA "Administrator of NASA") in the [Biden administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biden_administration "Biden administration") (then-Administrator [James Bridenstine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Bridenstine "James Bridenstine") had indicated that he did not intend to stay in the role under Biden, even if asked).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-16)

On April 16, 2021, the White House announced their intent to nominate Melroy to be NASA's deputy administrator, under former Democratic Senator [Bill Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Nelson "Bill Nelson"), who was nominated by the White House on March 19, 2021, to be the agency's administrator.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-17) On April 22, 2021, her nomination was sent to the Senate.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-18) The [Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Commerce,_Science,_and_Transportation "United States Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation") held a hearing on May 20, 2021, in which Melroy won strong bipartisan support to be deputy administrator. During her hearing, Melroy expressed support for extending the lifetime of the International Space Station, and said she would work closely with Nelson in running the agency.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-19)

On June 16, 2021, Melroy's nomination was reported out of the [Senate Commerce Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_Commerce_Committee "Senate Commerce Committee") by voice vote and the following day, she was confirmed by the full [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") with [unanimous consent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unanimous_consent "Unanimous consent").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-20) On June 21, 2021, Melroy was sworn into office by administrator [Bill Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Nelson "Bill Nelson").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-21) Melroy served as NASA deputy administrator through the end of the [Biden Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biden_Administration "Biden Administration"), leaving office January 20, 2025. On April 25, 2025, Melroy was honored with the National Space Trophy by the Rotary National Award for Space Achievement Foundation,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-22) and in September 2025, it was announced that Melroy was appointed to the Board of Directors for Venus Aerospace.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-23)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Pamela_Melroy&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Melroy is married to Douglas Hollett, a geologist, who was previously acting [assistant secretary for fossil energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_Secretary_for_Fossil_Energy "Assistant Secretary for Fossil Energy") in the [United States Department of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Energy "United States Department of Energy") and vice president for Southeast Asia exploration at [Marathon Oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_Oil "Marathon Oil").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Melroy#cite_note-:0-14)

**George David "Zambo" Zamka** (born June 29, 1962) is a former [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")[astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut") and [United States Marine Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps")[pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_aviator "Naval aviator") with over 3500 flight hours in more than 30 different aircraft. Zamka piloted the [Space Shuttle _Discovery_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery") in its October 2007 mission to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") and served as the commander of mission [STS-130](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-130 "STS-130") in February 2010.

## Personal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal")]

George David Zamka was born on June 29, 1962, at Margaret Hague Hospital in [Jersey City, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey_City,_New_Jersey "Jersey City, New Jersey").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-:0-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-2) He was raised in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"); [Irvington, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irvington,_New_York "Irvington, New York"); [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), Colombia;[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-Mom-3) and [Rochester Hills, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochester_Hills,_Michigan "Rochester Hills, Michigan"). He graduated from [Rochester Adams High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochester_Adams_High_School "Rochester Adams High School") in Michigan in 1980. His personal hobbies include weightlifting, running, bicycling, scuba diving, and boating.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-4)

Zamka is married and has two children. His extended family resides in Colorado, Mississippi, Georgia, Indiana, Florida and Tennessee. Zamka is of [Colombian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_people "Colombian people")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-6) and [Polish ancestry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_American "Polish American").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-rhg-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-9)

## Military career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Military career")]

Zamka graduated with a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in [mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics "Mathematics") from the [United States Naval Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Naval_Academy "United States Naval Academy") in 1984. He was then commissioned as a second lieutenant in the [United States Marine Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps"). He received [A-6E Intruder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-6_Intruder "A-6 Intruder") training at [Naval Air Station Whidbey Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Air_Station_Whidbey_Island "Naval Air Station Whidbey Island"), [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)") in 1985–1987. He was assigned to [VMA(AW)-242](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VMA(AW)-242 "VMA(AW)-242") at [Marine Corps Air Station El Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Corps_Air_Station_El_Toro "Marine Corps Air Station El Toro"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"). In addition to flight safety and administration, he was a squadron weapons and tactics instructor. In 1990, he trained as an [F/A-18D Hornet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F/A-18 "F/A-18") pilot and was then assigned to [VMFA(AW)-121](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VMFA(AW)-121 "VMFA(AW)-121"). Zamka flew 66 combat missions during [Operation Desert Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Desert_Storm "Operation Desert Storm"). In 1993, he was assigned to the [1st Battalion, 5th Marines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Battalion,_5th_Marines "1st Battalion, 5th Marines") at [Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Corps_Base_Camp_Pendleton "Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton"), California as a [forward air controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_air_controller "Forward air controller"). In December 1994, he graduated from the [U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Air_Force_Test_Pilot_School "U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School"), following which, he served as an [F/A-18 Hornet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F/A-18_Hornet "F/A-18 Hornet") test pilot and operations officer.

In 1997, he earned a Masters of Science degree in engineering management from the [Florida Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Institute_of_Technology "Florida Institute of Technology"). In 1998, he returned to VMFA(AW)-121 and deployed to [MCAS Iwakuni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MCAS_Iwakuni "MCAS Iwakuni"), Japan.

In August 2010, Zamka retired from the Marine Corps after almost 30 years of distinguished service. During his time as a pilot for the Marine Corps, Zamka logged more than 5,000 flight hours spanning 30 different aircraft.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-:1-10)As of May 2018[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit) he is [chairman of the board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_board "Chairman of the board") of the [National Association of Spaceports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Association_of_Spaceports?action=edit&redlink=1 "National Association of Spaceports (page does not exist)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-11)

## NASA career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NASA career")]

In June 1998, Zamka was selected for the NASA astronaut program, and reported for training in August. He served as lead for the Shuttle training and procedures division and as supervisor for the astronaut candidate class of 2004. Zamka made his first spaceflight as the pilot of mission STS-120, and second as the commander for [STS-130](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-130 "STS-130"). In March 2013, Zamka decided to retire from NASA.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-12)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-:0-1) In the two shuttle missions Zamka completed, he logged more than 692 hours in space and travelled 12 million miles.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-:0-1)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-:1-10)

## Honors and awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Honors and awards")]

Zamka has received the following honors and awards: the [Legion of Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legion_of_Merit "Legion of Merit"), [Distinguished Flying Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distinguished_Flying_Cross_(United_States) "Distinguished Flying Cross (United States)"), [Defense Meritorious Service Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_Meritorious_Service_Medal "Defense Meritorious Service Medal"), [Meritorious Service Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meritorious_Service_Medal_(United_States) "Meritorious Service Medal (United States)"), [Navy Strike Air Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Medal "Air Medal") (6), [Navy Commendation Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_Commendation_Medal "Navy Commendation Medal") with [Combat "V"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combat_%22V%22 "Combat \"V\""), and various other military service and campaign awards. Distinguished Graduate, U.S. Naval Academy. Commodore's list and Academic Achievement Award, Training Air Wing Five. Recipient of the [NASA Outstanding Leadership Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Outstanding_Leadership_Medal "NASA Outstanding Leadership Medal"), two [NASA Space Flight Medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Space_Flight_Medal "NASA Space Flight Medal"), four NASA Superior Accomplishment Awards and the GEM Award. He received also Officer's Cross of the [Order of Merit of the Republic of Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Merit_of_the_Republic_of_Poland "Order of Merit of the Republic of Poland") (2010).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-14)

## Promotional activities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Promotional activities")]

In March 2008, Zamka visited Colombia's [Planetarium of Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetarium_of_Bogot%C3%A1 "Planetarium of Bogotá") with the crew of mission STS-120 to share their experience as NASA astronauts with 200 students, 50 teachers, and 20 science major experts.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-15)

**George David "Zambo" Zamka** (born June 29, 1962) is a former [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")[astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut") and [United States Marine Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps")[pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_aviator "Naval aviator") with over 3500 flight hours in more than 30 different aircraft. Zamka piloted the [Space Shuttle _Discovery_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle_Discovery "Space Shuttle Discovery") in its October 2007 mission to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") and served as the commander of mission [STS-130](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-130 "STS-130") in February 2010.

## Personal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Personal")]

George David Zamka was born on June 29, 1962, at Margaret Hague Hospital in [Jersey City, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey_City,_New_Jersey "Jersey City, New Jersey").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-:0-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-2) He was raised in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"); [Irvington, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irvington,_New_York "Irvington, New York"); [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), Colombia;[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-Mom-3) and [Rochester Hills, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochester_Hills,_Michigan "Rochester Hills, Michigan"). He graduated from [Rochester Adams High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochester_Adams_High_School "Rochester Adams High School") in Michigan in 1980. His personal hobbies include weightlifting, running, bicycling, scuba diving, and boating.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-4)

Zamka is married and has two children. His extended family resides in Colorado, Mississippi, Georgia, Indiana, Florida and Tennessee. Zamka is of [Colombian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_people "Colombian people")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-6) and [Polish ancestry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_American "Polish American").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-rhg-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-9)

## Military career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Military career")]

Zamka graduated with a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in [mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics "Mathematics") from the [United States Naval Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Naval_Academy "United States Naval Academy") in 1984. He was then commissioned as a second lieutenant in the [United States Marine Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps"). He received [A-6E Intruder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-6_Intruder "A-6 Intruder") training at [Naval Air Station Whidbey Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Air_Station_Whidbey_Island "Naval Air Station Whidbey Island"), [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)") in 1985–1987. He was assigned to [VMA(AW)-242](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VMA(AW)-242 "VMA(AW)-242") at [Marine Corps Air Station El Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Corps_Air_Station_El_Toro "Marine Corps Air Station El Toro"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"). In addition to flight safety and administration, he was a squadron weapons and tactics instructor. In 1990, he trained as an [F/A-18D Hornet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F/A-18 "F/A-18") pilot and was then assigned to [VMFA(AW)-121](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VMFA(AW)-121 "VMFA(AW)-121"). Zamka flew 66 combat missions during [Operation Desert Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Desert_Storm "Operation Desert Storm"). In 1993, he was assigned to the [1st Battalion, 5th Marines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Battalion,_5th_Marines "1st Battalion, 5th Marines") at [Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Corps_Base_Camp_Pendleton "Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton"), California as a [forward air controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_air_controller "Forward air controller"). In December 1994, he graduated from the [U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Air_Force_Test_Pilot_School "U.S. Air Force Test Pilot School"), following which, he served as an [F/A-18 Hornet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F/A-18_Hornet "F/A-18 Hornet") test pilot and operations officer.

In 1997, he earned a Masters of Science degree in engineering management from the [Florida Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Institute_of_Technology "Florida Institute of Technology"). In 1998, he returned to VMFA(AW)-121 and deployed to [MCAS Iwakuni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MCAS_Iwakuni "MCAS Iwakuni"), Japan.

In August 2010, Zamka retired from the Marine Corps after almost 30 years of distinguished service. During his time as a pilot for the Marine Corps, Zamka logged more than 5,000 flight hours spanning 30 different aircraft.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-:1-10)As of May 2018[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit) he is [chairman of the board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_board "Chairman of the board") of the [National Association of Spaceports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Association_of_Spaceports?action=edit&redlink=1 "National Association of Spaceports (page does not exist)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-11)

## NASA career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: NASA career")]

In June 1998, Zamka was selected for the NASA astronaut program, and reported for training in August. He served as lead for the Shuttle training and procedures division and as supervisor for the astronaut candidate class of 2004. Zamka made his first spaceflight as the pilot of mission STS-120, and second as the commander for [STS-130](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-130 "STS-130"). In March 2013, Zamka decided to retire from NASA.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-12)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-:0-1) In the two shuttle missions Zamka completed, he logged more than 692 hours in space and travelled 12 million miles.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-:0-1)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-:1-10)

## Honors and awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Honors and awards")]

Zamka has received the following honors and awards: the [Legion of Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legion_of_Merit "Legion of Merit"), [Distinguished Flying Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distinguished_Flying_Cross_(United_States) "Distinguished Flying Cross (United States)"), [Defense Meritorious Service Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_Meritorious_Service_Medal "Defense Meritorious Service Medal"), [Meritorious Service Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meritorious_Service_Medal_(United_States) "Meritorious Service Medal (United States)"), [Navy Strike Air Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Medal "Air Medal") (6), [Navy Commendation Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_Commendation_Medal "Navy Commendation Medal") with [Combat "V"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combat_%22V%22 "Combat \"V\""), and various other military service and campaign awards. Distinguished Graduate, U.S. Naval Academy. Commodore's list and Academic Achievement Award, Training Air Wing Five. Recipient of the [NASA Outstanding Leadership Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Outstanding_Leadership_Medal "NASA Outstanding Leadership Medal"), two [NASA Space Flight Medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Space_Flight_Medal "NASA Space Flight Medal"), four NASA Superior Accomplishment Awards and the GEM Award. He received also Officer's Cross of the [Order of Merit of the Republic of Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Merit_of_the_Republic_of_Poland "Order of Merit of the Republic of Poland") (2010).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-14)

## Promotional activities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_D._Zamka&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Promotional activities")]

In March 2008, Zamka visited Colombia's [Planetarium of Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetarium_of_Bogot%C3%A1 "Planetarium of Bogotá") with the crew of mission STS-120 to share their experience as NASA astronauts with 200 students, 50 teachers, and 20 science major experts.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_D._Zamka#cite_note-15)
